<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Stores the ReplaySSM ring trackers in the Mamba page and puts the dt ring last, which removes `MambaSpec.state_alignment`. Stacked on #55688 and drafted until it merges: until then the diff includes its commits, so review the last two commits. Needs [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8548](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8548) (strided trackers) and a FlashInfer release that contains it.

## Claims

- The per-slot `(ring_start, num_committed)` trackers are a sixth Mamba state. Block copies, the align pre-copy and KV cache accounting cover them, so the off-page tracker allocation, binding, block-copy tensors and cleanup are removed from both model runners, the extensible KV cache and the worker utils.
- The page order is conv, ssm, x, B, dt, trackers. FlashInfer's 16-byte-sensitive states (ssm, x, B) start aligned without per-state padding, so `MambaSpec.state_alignment` is removed. A one-time check raises a clear error if a layout would misalign them.
- On Nemotron-3.5 Lightning NVFP4, GSM8K accuracy, MTP acceptance and prefix-cache hits match #55688 within run-to-run variation.
- Serving performance is unchanged within measurement resolution: with MTP acceptance and MoE routing fixed, the output-throughput change is between −0.34% and +0.05% at concurrency 1–32, with 95% confidence intervals inside [−1.05%, +0.44%], and −0.13% [−1.33%, +1.07%] at 64. nsys shows the only added GPU time is ~0.1% of a step, from the per-layer tracker copies and writes.

## Validation

**E2E:** Nemotron-3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B NVFP4, one B200, V2 model runner, FlashInfer ReplaySSM (`--replayssm-buffer-len 16`), FP16 SSM state with stochastic rounding (5 Philox rounds), MTP3, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching with `--prefix-match-unit 326` (the Mamba block is 2608 tokens). Baseline is #55688's head `a8877fadf6`; both runs use FlashInfer with [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8548](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8548) and the same server command.

GSM8K: two runs per side, each with its own server start; values are means with the range in brackets.

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, five shots, greedy, concurrency 64:

| | Accuracy | Mean acceptance length | Prefix-hit tokens (each run) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #55688 | 85.45% [85.4–85.5] | 3.439 | 859,336 of 958,923 |
| This PR | 84.55% [84.5–84.6] | 3.444 | 859,336 of 958,923 |

The GSM8K difference is within run-to-run variation: even without stochastic rounding, at concurrency 1, two runs of #55688 give identical completions for only 95 of the first 200 questions (85.5% and 85.0%). This PR matches them on 88 and 86 (84.5%). Both sides hit the prefix cache for the same 129,748 of 145,415 tokens.

Serving, output throughput of this PR relative to #55688:

| Concurrency | Change | 95% CI | Server starts per side |
|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | +0.05% | [−0.06%, +0.15%] | 6 |
| 8 | −0.34% | [−0.68%, +0.00%] | 10 |
| 32 | −0.31% | [−1.05%, +0.44%] | 10 |
| 64 | −0.13% | [−1.33%, +1.07%] | 6 |

For scale, #55688 serves 849 / 2,814 / 5,687 / 7,794 output tok/s at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 on one node. How the runs were made low-noise:

- Same work per step on both sides: MTP acceptance fixed by synthetic rejection sampling at the acceptance length measured above (`"rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 3.441`), MoE routing fixed with `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, greedy sampling, `--ignore-eos`.
- Random prompts around 1024 in / 512 out with per-request lengths (`--random-range-ratio 0.5`), seeded identically on both sides. With fixed lengths, requests move in lockstep and throughput at concurrency 32 varied by up to 5% between identical runs.
- An untimed warm-up, then each point with its own seed, so later points do not hit the prefix cache from earlier ones.
- A whole B200 node per run, with the server and client pinned to the GPU's NUMA node. On a shared node, identical runs varied by up to 6%.
- Server starts interleaved between the two sides on two nodes, two repeats per start, compared per seed. Identical runs of #55688 on one node agree within 0.0–2.0%.

nsys (benchmark window only, c = 8 and 64) shows the same total GPU kernel time on both sides (−0.05%, +0.30%). The PR's two Mamba bookkeeping kernels are slower, `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` by 17–20% and `postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel` by 16–19%, as they now copy and write the trackers of every layer: about 3 µs per step at concurrency 8 and 20 µs at 64, roughly 0.1% of a step.

<details>
<summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --use-replayssm --replayssm-buffer-len 16 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 326 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# Serving runs add to the speculative config:
#   "rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.441
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
# Serving runs also set VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random on the server.
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.5 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts {64,256,512,1024} --max-concurrency {1,8,32,64} --seed {1001,1008,1032,1064}
# Second repeat per server start: seeds 2001, 2008, 2032, 2064.
```
</details>

**Unit tests** (B200): `tests/kernels/mamba/test_ssu_dispatch.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends_selection.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_replayssm_warmup.py`: 192 passed, 1 skipped. `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py`: 105 passed, 12 failed; the same 12 `s32_a32` cases fail on #55688's head (FP32 tolerance).

**Not tested:** MRV1 end to end, the Triton ReplaySSM backend end to end, TP > 1, and GSM8K without prefix caching.

## Details

- Each layer's page holds its own copy of the group's trackers. The ReplaySSM kernels read a group's first layer and write all of its layers: `num_layers × num_reqs` int32 stores per step instead of `num_groups × num_reqs`.
- The fresh-slot reset now runs after the align pre-copy, in V1 and V2. The pre-copy copies a continuing slot's page, trackers included, and reads the null block when a group has no source; resetting afterwards keeps fresh slots at zero.
- The Triton decode planner takes a strided `ring_pos` and indexes it in 64 bits.
- Alignment relies on hybrid models padding the Mamba page to the attention page, a multiple of 16. A layout that misaligns ssm, x or B now fails at startup instead of being padded per state.
- The tracker offset in FlashInfer uses 32-bit operands with a 64-bit product; vLLM's FlashInfer pin is unchanged until a release includes [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8548](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8548). With the current pin, FlashInfer rejects the strided trackers (`ring_start must be contiguous`).
- Size: source +222 / −198 lines, tests +120 / −201.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Read the served block size from the startup log. 64 is a reasonable starting point.
 
+### FlashInfer ReplaySSM
+
+FlashInfer ReplaySSM caches recent inputs to reduce full-state writes during Mamba2 decoding. It is disabled by default. Both Model Runners V1 and V2 support prefix caching with ReplaySSM, including MTP speculative decoding.
+
+This example enables ReplaySSM and prefix caching with three MTP draft tokens:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --max-model-len 12288 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --mamba-backend flashinfer \
+    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
+    --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \
+    --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
+    --use-replayssm \
+    --replayssm-buffer-len 16 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
+```
+
+`--enable-prefix-caching` selects Mamba cache mode `align`. To use ReplaySSM without prefix caching, replace this flag with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. This selects mode `none`. To disable speculative decoding, remove `--speculative-config`.
+
+FlashInfer ReplaySSM has these limits:
+
+- `align` requires BF16 model inputs for its replay rings. The SSM state dtype is independent. The example uses FP16 state with stochastic rounding.
+- The logical replay buffer cannot exceed 16 tokens. For speculative decoding, it must contain at least `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens.
+- Pipeline parallelism, microbatching, and KV connectors are not supported.
+
+Prefix reuse still requires a shared prefix with a saved Mamba checkpoint. The matching rules for hybrid Mamba models above also apply.
+

+def assign_replayssm_decode_planners(
+    kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> None:
+    """Pick, per cache group, the layer that plans each Triton decode step.
+
+    The ring trackers live in each layer's Mamba page (state 5), so block copies,
+    the align pre-copy and KV cache accounting handle them like the rings.
+    """
+    for group in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups:
+        names = [
+            name
+            for name in group.layer_names
+            if isinstance(layer := forward_context.get(name), MambaBase)
+            and layer.use_replayssm
+        ]
+        if not names:
+            continue
+        for name in names:
+            forward_context[name]._plans_replayssm_decode = False
+        # Triton plans each decode step in the group's first executed layer.
+        planner = min(names, key=extract_layer_index)
+        forward_context[planner]._plans_replayssm_decode = True

+def _reinterpret_u64_as_i64(value: int) -> int:
+    """Preserve a uint64 pointer bit pattern in a torch.int64 tensor."""
+    return value if value < (1 << 63) else value - (1 << 64)
+

+@triton.jit
+def _tracker_row(tracker_ptrs, tracker_slot_strides, layer, slot):
+    """Address of a slot's (ring_start, num_committed) pair in a layer's page."""
+    base = tl.load(tracker_ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+    # Page-sized slot strides: index in 64 bits.
+    return base + slot.to(tl.int64) * tl.load(tracker_slot_strides + layer)

+    tracker_slot_strides,

+    num_layers,

+    start,
+    committed,
+    mask,

+    """Write a slot's trackers to every layer of a cache group."""
+    for layer in range(first_layer, first_layer + num_layers):
+        row = _tracker_row(tracker_ptrs, tracker_slot_strides, layer, slot)
+        tl.store(row, start, mask=mask)
+        tl.store(row + 1, committed, mask=mask)

+    aligned_new_computed = (new_num_computed // block_size) * block_size

+    accept_token_bias = aligned_new_computed - num_tokens_running_state
+    dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1
+    return needs_copy, accept_token_bias, dest_block_idx
